_: THE CLAUDE-STATE PARITY CORPUS. One file, two readers: server/tests/state_parity.rs (chat::parser + chat::agent_error) and web/tests/unit/chat-state-parity.test.ts (agent-error.ts + wire-entries.ts). Every row is a VERBATIM Claude Code payload captured off this box (or, where marked, transcribed from the 2.1.227 binary's own template strings) together with what both planes must make of it. Fields: name; line (the raw JSONL transcript record, exactly as CC writes it); expect.kind / expect.label / expect.ok (what the Rust parser must produce); expect.body (a SUBSET of the wire body - every key listed must match exactly); expect.display (optional: the display kind web/wire-entries.ts must render, '-' meaning deliberately not rendered). Why a shared file: the limit taxonomy is classified on BOTH planes - the server stamps it onto the wire entry, the client re-derives it from a StopFailure banner for the roster badge - and neither language errors when the two drift. A session that is dead for five hours rendered as an ordinary speech bubble because nothing held them together.
